title: Universal MAT core — stage 1
body:
# Universal MAT core — stage 1

The [3 October source-bound material continuation](13-Source-Bound-Materials.md) adds one alloy owner (191 universal projections), typed source-metrology context and a reviewed composition/process/API round trip. The original stage below remains an architecture checkpoint, not a claim of scientific completeness.

## 13 October continuation — neutral atomic Hydrogen

The [explicit atomic adapter](../../scripts/mat-atomic.mjs) reuses `MAT:0001:ATOM:H`, already owned by [Hydrogen's structured record](../../records/0001-Hydrogen-H/data/structured/0001-Hydrogen-H.yaml) at `/charge_states/1`, charge zero. The additive `ATOM` class describes this existing neutral species separately from the elemental parent, ions and H2. The generic catalogue now contains 192 objects; all generic reading lists remain empty. The original 191 projections retain their contents and order.

The separate `/atoms` read-only query endpoint and `node scripts/mat-query-service.mjs --atoms --pretty` command return one explicit source-bound example. It reuses the existing `/ionization/first` value and [binding `/bindings/0`](../../data/research/mat-dashboard-bindings.json). The existing `/readings` five-reading payload and `/materials` payload stay compatible. [Universal validation](../../scripts/validate-universal-core.mjs) and the [master-update intake](../../data/quality/mat-update-intake.json) expose it separately as `atomic_examples`.

The retained [NIST ASD 5.12 export](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-asd-ionisation-2026-09-14.csv), physical row 2, [extraction provenance](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-asd-ionisation-2026-09-14.provenance.json) and [official help snapshot](../../data/catalog/sources/nist-asd-ionisation-help-2026-09-14.html) are checked by their reviewed SHA-256 hashes. [NIST's live definitions](https://physics.nist.gov/PhysRefData/ASD/Html/iehelp.html) and [database DOI](https://doi.org/10.18434/T4W30F) remain external source destinations. Parentheses retain THEORETICAL evidence; displayed eV uncertainty is preserved without inventing confidence or coverage. The raw source bibliography key `HDEL` is distinct from source `SRC-000005`; underlying-work and claim-level review remain open, and rights remain UNKNOWN.

The typed reading's `state_ref` is the existing file locator `records/0001-Hydrogen-H/data/structured/0001-Hydrogen-H.yaml#/electronic_ground_state`. The adapter checks configuration `1s1` and term `2S1/2` against the retained one-electron source notation `1s` and `2S<1/2>`. This locator does not allocate a permanent state child. The object's complete state stays `state_ref: null`, `status: UNRESOLVED`; isotope, temperature, pressure, frame, time, validity, scientific confidence and coverage factor remain unknown. The owner confidence label A is preserved only as a legacy qualifier.

The [atomic regressions](../../scripts/tests/mat-atomic.test.mjs) exercise persisted wrong-owner/species/charge/H2 fixtures, binding/pointer/unit/source/state drift, changed values and uncertainties, evidence promotion, source snapshot changes and the read-only API. This is a bounded software/source-binding bridge under existing task 130 and Hydrogen's ionisation-ladder task. It does not close the whole domain, element, claim review or 22-image requirement.

Subsequent bounded route research identifies HDEL as a [NIST Energy Levels of Hydrogen and Deuterium website/resource reference](https://www.nist.gov/pml/energy-levels-hydrogen-and-deuterium), confirmed by the [official website bibliography record](https://www.nist.gov/publications/energy-levels-hydrogen-and-deuterium-0). Its current destination displays an updating notice without calculation-version documentation. NIST’s [Precision Frequencies theory documentation](https://www.nist.gov/programs-projects/quantum-physics-theory) links a related [2005 primary-paper record](https://www.nist.gov/publications/precise-calculation-transition-frequencies-hydrogen-and-deuterium-based-least-squares), [DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.163003](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.163003). Later bounded research retrieved and inspected all four pages of the [complete original paper from NIST](https://www.nist.gov/document/physrevlett95163003pdf), with exact raw bytes, SHA-256 and page/line locators retained in private review evidence. It documents the 2002 CODATA adjustment and finite bound-state transition-frequency tables in kHz. It does not print or establish the exact retained ionisation-energy/uncertainty pair or the dated 2026 ASD row’s calculation/constants version. Paper-specific standard uncertainty, covariance and hyperfine conventions are not transferred to that row. This remains a related-method reference; no canonical numeric replacement follows. Exact row-to-calculation, state, uncertainty and reuse linkage remains UNVERIFIED. No new source ID or scientific admission follows from these links.

The next source trace preserves six complete official responses with raw hashes and exact locators. The [original 107-page CODATA 2002 review](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/pdf/CODATA_RMP2005.pdf), linked by the [2002 archive](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/archive2002.html), is historical methodology. The [least-squares data page](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/LSAData/index.html) identifies the 2002 adjustment; listed numerical matrices remain routes only. The [constants version history](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Reference/versioncon.shtml) dates Web 4.1 to 18 April 2005, providing the adjustment data, and Web 4.2 to 24 May 2005, improving correlation accuracy and correcting residuals Y. It separately dates Web 9.0 to 9 May 2024 for the 2022 constants. These are distinct revision scopes, with historical rounded isotope-specific numbers kept outside the canonical Hydrogen projection. All 107 pages were extracted and searched; scientific reading covered the relevant identity, historical table provenance, Appendix A introduction and unit/uncertainty sections, with extraction limits retained.

The [ASD version history](https://physics.nist.gov/PhysRefData/ASD/Html/verhist.shtml) dates ASD 5.12 to 7 November 2024 and identifies its energy-conversion constants as 2022 CODATA, Web Version 9.0, accessed 19 October 2024. This establishes release-level conversion context. The [conversion documentation](https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/energy.html) links a 2022 factor table; the linked factor table was not retrieved, and the captured conversion form was not executed in this slice. The retained ionisation help describes stored `cm^-1` data and output uncertainty combining the stored-data and conversion-factor uncertainties in quadrature before rounding. Exact retained-row native calculation, adjustment/QED/constants revision, unrounded native uncertainty, isotope convention, covariance applicability and conversion execution remain UNVERIFIED. Source-specific rights remain UNKNOWN. No canonical recalculation, scientific value, source/owner/state identity or panel credit follows. The dated native-row evidence dependency remains open while the existing catalogue intake can advance using its saved NIST/CERN page 14 requests.

This additive implementation reconciles the owner request from “Test a theory” (conversation `6abb2347-aad4-83eb-b5c6-7db40831a19e`) with the existing 143-section master update, accession SRC-000342. The conversation connector returned five turns, with its long master-prompt message truncated at 20,000 characters. The complete locally accessioned 4,878-line update remains the reference for section locators; this is not a claim of a complete conversation export.

## Existing owners and migration

The [universal schema](01-Universal-Schema.md), [identifier system](03-Identifier-System.md), [claim registry](10-Claim-Registry.md), epistemic graph, canonical records, proposed catalogue and MAT-TODO queue remain authoritative. The legacy parent-record schema describes the current recognised catalogue, including its 118 bound. That scope is not a universal ontology limit.

The new [object projection schema](../../data/schema/1.0.0/mat-universal-object.schema.json) wraps existing owners without rewriting them. [The adapter](../../scripts/mat-universal-object.mjs) resolves both existing structured layouts: top-level `mat_id` and nested `identity.mat_id`/`record_id`. Conflicting aliases fail. Identity recognition is checked against the existing catalogue; candidate entries keep `MAT-PROPOSED` identities. The contract accepts future candidate numbers without a 118 or 188 maximum. Recognition is never inferred from a number or promoted by schema validation. Expanding canonical recognised publication records still requires a separately reviewed catalogue/schema migration.

All current parent records inherit the same contract and point to the same universal requirements profile: Origin, Hydrogen through Oganesson, all current proposed identities, and the existing `MAT:0001:MOL:H2` object. The molecule remains owned by Hydrogen's structured record. Other supported object classes (materials, samples, processes, fields, biological systems and others) use existing child namespaces. This release demonstrates H2 plus synthetic material/process fixtures; it does not bulk-create other objects or redefine identifiers for sources, patents or claims. Those stay references to their existing registries.

This is a read-time migration. No original record, accepted value or identifier is rewritten. `loadOwner` records a path, JSON pointer and SHA-256; `verifyOwner` detects stale content and unresolved identities. Rebuild projections after owner changes. Schema validation establishes shape only; pointer hashes establish provenance integrity, not scientific truth.

## Common contract and evidence boundaries

Every projection exposes state, conditions, frame/time references, validity, readings, composition, ordered process genome, typed relationship references and the same three reading-layer slots. Empty collections/null state mean **unreviewed or unresolved**, never known absence or zero. The adapter deliberately does not guess state-specific readings from heterogeneous legacy numbers.

- `MAT_RAW`: references to canonical owners only; no second numeric database.
- `MAT_VECTOR`: `NOT-COMPUTED`. Unit-aware normalisation and missing-value masks require a future reviewed transformation contract.
- `MAT_FINGERPRINT`: `NOT-COMPUTED`. No scalar “frequency of an element,” embedding or physical fingerprint is fabricated. Provenance SHA-256 is not a physical fingerprint.

The measurement shape retains a unit, state, optional frame, explicit uncertainty/null status, validity and provenance. Measured, evaluated, calculated/derived, simulated, theoretical, predicted, historical, philosophical, religious/traditional, speculative, disputed, falsified, fictional, authored and unverified lanes remain distinct. No conversion into the older claim-registry status vocabulary is automatic. Scalar metric names can cover mass, volume, density, thermal, electrical, magnetic, mechanical, wave and quantum quantities; vector/tensor/spatial series representations and full metrology remain pending. Dynamics and time-dilation-labelled readings require a frame reference; this does not implement reference-frame transformations or relativity. A frame name alone does not qualify a model.

Process steps reference inputs, outputs, parameters and provenance, retaining array order. Typed links cover composition/process/structure/property/performance/failure, products, co-products, by-products, residuals, heat, evidence and research. This gives process history and circular-matter work a shared place to attach evidence. It does not prove conservation, recoverability, safety, causal relationships or lifecycle feasibility. Complete process curves and multiphysics models remain pending.

## Composition engine

[Composition arithmetic](../../scripts/mat-composition.mjs) validates `wt%`, `at%`, `mol%`, `vol%`, `ppm`, `ppb`, `phase_fraction` and `isotope_fraction`. Every input declares a compatible MASS, ATOM_COUNT, AMOUNT or VOLUME basis and COMPLETE or PARTIAL coverage. Phase and isotope populations remain distinct. Values must be finite and nonnegative, references unique, totals at most one normalised whole, and complete totals equal one within a fixed 1e-12 numerical roundoff tolerance. This tolerance is not scientific uncertainty. Partial compositions report the unassigned fraction without filling it.

Conversions only rescale compatible units on the same basis. Mass-to-atomic, molecular/atomic, volume/mass and population changes require scientific inputs and are rejected here. No density, molar mass or phase model is assumed.

Multiple components can change together:

- `LOCK_REMAINDER`: an explicitly selected balance component receives the residual after requested changes; other components retain their values.
- `LOCK_RATIO`: remaining components retain their mutual ratios while filling the residual.
- `FREE_OPTIMISATION`: validates a caller-supplied complete balanced candidate. Despite the requested mode name, this does not perform optimisation.

Fixed stoichiometry refuses all adjustment requests. A different composition must be proposed as a different physical system. Results retain the original composition and changes, are tagged CALCULATED and arithmetic-only, explicitly report uncertainty not propagated, and return no property predictions. Test values are synthetic constraint examples, not a sourced steel recipe.

## Authored theory and image preservation

The [source accession](../../data/research/sources/mat-update-2026-09-29.txt) retains A/B/C/X meanings, the 12 original operators and 24 potential expressions. The validator extracts those exact sets from sections 32 and 33 without executing them. They remain AUTHOR-FRAMEWORK, separate from arithmetic and established physics; their presence is not an accepted causal model. Standard inverse-relation examples elsewhere in section 32 are not counted as authored operators.

The attached 29 September dashboard matches the existing SRC-000343 image exactly (SHA-256 `95d262aae03b6ab1a023de1d513693a926596538f861bf447e4081dcd93fd850`). It is a layout reference with rejected scientific data, including the fictional Primidium identity. No duplicate image, scientific value or rendering credit is added. Future visuals must consume validated canonical identities/readings; this stage creates no visuals.

## Requirement tracking and next acceptance

The existing review metadata and generated `MAT-TODO.json` contain the continuation and per-section partial progress. All 143 section acceptances remain OPEN. Existing scientific enrichment work resumes independently at Copper; no scientific review was completed by this tooling batch.

Current requirement: `MAT-UPDATE-20260929-018`, composition engine. Next: select one documented variable-composition material/sample, resolve its canonical owner, source, fraction basis, state, uncertainty and validity; attach a reviewed composition and process history and validate a round trip. Reuse the existing material/process templates. Do not label synthetic fixtures as real materials.

This is the 29 September stage checkpoint. The [3 October knowledge-integration continuation](../09-production/MAT-Knowledge-Integration-2026-10-03.md) advances the existing Hydrogen reader/API acceptance slice (current task 130); composition task 018 remains open. The exported validator now enforces recognised-catalogue membership and optional explicit scale context.

Still pending: physically justified cross-basis conversions and uncertainty propagation; numeric vectors/fingerprints; dimensional equation and conservation gates; reference-frame transforms and relativity models; spatial fields/multiphysics; general optimisation, extremes, Pareto, sensitivity/tolerance; reverse engineering and lost-material reconstruction; biomimetic mechanism mappings; patent/prior-art/negative-result ingestion; discovery/inverse design/matter compiler and their acceptance evidence. These retain the existing section tasks rather than becoming a competing backlog.

## Reproduction

Run `npm run validate:universal` for canonical coverage and authored-string preservation, or `node scripts/validate-universal-core.mjs --json` for the full reproducible projection. Run `node --test scripts/tests/mat-universal-core.test.mjs` for positive and rejection-path tests. The universal validator also participates in `npm run validate`. No CLI writes to canonical records.
